title: Battleships in a Board Problem

notes: Each battleship is counted exactly once at its top-leftmost cell.
Because distinct battleships are separated horizontally or vertically, an X is a ship start exactly when the cell above and the cell to its left are not X.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]
content.problemStatement:
With an `m x n` matrix `board` where each cell is a battleship `'X'` or empty `'.'`, output *the number of the **battleships** on* `board`.

**Battleships** can only be placed horizontally or vertically on `board`. In other words, they can only be made of the shape `1 x k` (`1` row, `k` columns) or `k x 1` (`k` rows, `1` column), where `k` can be of any size. At least one horizontal or vertical cell separates between two battleships (i.e., there are no adjacent battleships).

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2024/06/21/image.png)

```
Input: board = [["X",".",".","X"],[".",".",".","X"],[".",".",".","X"]]
Output: 2
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: board = [["."]]
Output: 0
```

**Constraints:**

* `m == board.length`
* `n == board[i].length`
* `1 <= m, n <= 200`
* `board[i][j]` is either `'.'` or `'X'`.

**Follow up:** Could you do it in one-pass, using only `O(1)` extra memory and without modifying the values `board`?

notes: Expected output is the JSON-serialised integer returned by countBattleships.

solution.approach: Scan the board once and count an X only when the cell above it and the cell to its left are not X.

better.complexity: O(m*n) time and O(m*n) auxiliary space.
better.description: Scan the board while marking visited ship cells in an auxiliary matrix.

optimal.complexity: O(m*n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Count only ship-start cells whose upper and left neighbors are not X. The guaranteed separation makes this sufficient.

bruteForce.complexity: O(m*n) time and O(m*n) auxiliary space.
bruteForce.description: Use DFS/BFS from each unvisited X cell to count connected components.

followUps: What changes if diagonal touching were also forbidden?
How would you count ships with DFS instead?
Can the same idea work in a streaming row-by-row implementation?

hidden.label: Two vertical ships and one single

learningObjectives: Recognize local invariants in a matrix.
Count components without extra visited storage.
Use problem guarantees to simplify traversal.
